Built-in evaluators list and usage\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Why Critical**: Without proper SDK understanding, you risk:\r\n- Implementing unnecessary custom evaluators when built-ins exist\r\n- Incorrect evaluator structure leading to runtime errors\r\n- Improper data formatting causing evaluation failures\r\n- Missing key SDK features that optimize performance\r\n\r\n## Core Principles\r\n\r\n- Use Azure AI Evaluation SDK (azure-ai-evaluation)\r\n- Generate a plan before writing code\r\n\r\n## Implement Evaluators\r\n\r\n### Understanding Evaluator Architecture\r\n\r\nAll evaluators in Azure AI Evaluation SDK follow a consistent class structure with two essential methods:\r\n\r\n| Method | Purpose | Details |\r\n|--------|---------|---------|\r\n| `__init__()` | **Setup** | Initializes evaluator with configuration (model settings, parameters, file paths) |\r\n| `__call__()` | **Evaluation Logic** | Processes inputs from your data and returns evaluation results |\r\n\r\n### Choose Your Evaluator Type\r\n\r\nAzure AI Evaluation SDK supports three types of evaluators:\r\n\r\n| Type | Best For | Complexity | Priority |\r\n|------|----------|------------|----------|\r\n| **🔌 Built-in** | Common AI metrics (task adherence, intent resolution, tool accuracy, etc.) | Low | **1st Choice** |\r\n| **🔧 Custom Code-based** | Business-specific objective metrics with custom logic | Medium | 2nd Choice |\r\n| **🤖 Custom Prompt-based** | Business-specific subjective metrics requiring LLM judgment | High | 3rd Choice |\r\n\r\nFor each evaluator you need to implement, follow this decision tree:\r\n\r\n1. **Check Built-in Evaluators First**: Always start by checking if your evaluator can be satisfied via SDK's built-in evaluators\r\n   - ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Create evaluators\r\ntask_adherence_evaluator = TaskAdherenceEvaluator(model_config=model_config) # built-in evaluator\r\nanswer_length_evaluator = AnswerLengthEvaluator() # custom code-based evaluator\r\nfriendliness_evaluator = FriendlinessEvaluator(model_config)\r\n\r\n\r\n# 5. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

Extract tool names from tool calls\\n        weather_tools = []\\n        time_tools = []\\n        other_tools = []\\n        \\n        for call in tool_calls:\\n            if isinstance(call, dict):\\n                name = call.get('name', '')\\n                if 'weather' in name.lower():\\n                    weather_tools.append(call)\\n                elif 'time' in name.lower():\\n                    time_tools.append(call)\\n                else:\\n                    other_tools.append(call)\\n        \\n        has_weather_call = len(weather_tools) > 0\\n        has_time_call = len(time_tools) > 0\\n        total_calls = len(tool_calls)\\n        \\n        # Score based on coordination quality\\n        score = 0.0\\n        reason_parts = []\\n        \\n        if has_weather_call and has_time_call:\\n            score += 3.0  # Base score for using both required tools\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Used both weather and time tools\\\")\\n            \\n            # Check for parallel execution (tools called in same LLM turn)\\n            if len(tool_calls) == 2:  # Optimal case: exactly 2 calls\\n                score += 2.0\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Optimal parallel execution\\\")\\n            elif len(tool_calls) > 2:\\n                score += 1.0  # Some points for parallel but with extra calls\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Parallel execution with extra calls\\\")\\n            else:\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Sequential execution\\\")\\n        elif has_weather_call or has_time_call:\\n            score += 1.0  # Partial score for using one required tool\\n            missing = \\\"time\\\" if has_weather_call else \\\"weather\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(f\\\"Missing {missing} tool call\\\")\\n        else:\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Missing both required tool calls\\\")\\n        \\n        # Efficiency rating\\n        if score >= 4.5:\\n            efficiency = \\\"excellent\\\"\\n        elif score >= 3.0:\\n            efficiency = \\\"good\\\"\\n        elif score >= 1.5:\\n            efficiency = \\\"fair\\\"\\n        else:\\n            efficiency = \\\"poor\\\"\\n        \\n        return {\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": efficiency,\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency_score\\\": score,\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency_reason\\\": \\\"; \\\".join(reason_parts)\\n        }\\n\\n\\nclass ResponseCompletenessEvaluator:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Evaluates whether the response includes both weather and time information when both are requested.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    def __init__(self):\\n        pass\\n    \\n    def __call__(self, *, query: str, response: str, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Union[str, float]]:\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Evaluate response completeness for weather-time coordination queries.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        query_lower = query.lower()\\n        response_lower = response.lower()\\n        \\n        # Check if query requests both weather and time\\n        needs_weather = any(word in query_lower for word in ['weather', 'temperature', 'sunny', 'rain', 'climate'])\\n        needs_time = any(word in query_lower for word in ['time', 'utc', 'clock', 'hour', 'minute', 'when'])\\n        \\n        if not (needs_weather and needs_time):\\n            return {\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": \\\"not_applicable\\\",\\n                \\\"response_completeness_score\\\": 0.0,\\n                \\\"response_completeness_reason\\\": \\\"Query does not require both weather and time\\\"\\n            }\\n        \\n        # Check if response contains weather information\\n        has_weather_info = any(word in response_lower for word in [\\n            'weather', 'temperature', 'sunny', 'rain', 'cloudy', 'degrees', '°c', '°f', 'celsius', 'fahrenheit'\\n        ])\\n        \\n        # Check if response contains time information\\n        has_time_info = any(word in response_lower for word in [\\n            'time', 'utc', 'am', 'pm', 'hour', 'minute', 'clock', ':', 'september', 'monday', 'tuesday'\\n        ]) or any(char.isdigit() and ':' in response for char in response)\\n        \\n        score = 0.0\\n        reason_parts = []\\n        \\n        if has_weather_info and has_time_info:\\n            score = 5.0\\n            completeness = \\\"complete\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Contains both weather and time information\\\")\\n        elif has_weather_info or has_time_info:\\n            score = 2.5\\n            completeness = \\\"partial\\\"\\n            missing = \\\"time\\\" if has_weather_info else \\\"weather\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(f\\\"Contains only {missing} information\\\")\\n        else:\\n            score = 0.0\\n            completeness = \\\"incomplete\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Missing both weather and time information\\\")\\n        \\n        return {\\n            \\\"response_completeness\\\": completeness,\\n            \\\"response_completeness_score\\\": score,\\n            \\\"response_completeness_reason\\\": \\\"; \\\".join(reason_parts)\\n        }\\n\\n\\ndef convert_traces_to_jsonl(traces_file: str, output_file: str) -> str:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Convert OpenTelemetry traces to JSONL format for evaluation.\\n    \\n    Args:\\n        traces_file: Path to the JSON file containing traces\\n        output_file: Path to save the JSONL file\\n    \\n    Returns:\\n        Path to the created JSONL file\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    with open(traces_file, 'r') as f:\\n        data = json.load(f)\\n    \\n    evaluation_data = []\\n    \\n    for trace in data.get('traces', []):\\n        # Extract query from user message event\\n        query = None\\n        response = None\\n        tool_calls = []\\n        \\n        for event in trace.get('events', []):\\n            if event['name'] == 'gen_ai.user.message':\\n                body = json.loads(event['body'])\\n                contents = body.get('contents', [])\\n                if contents and contents[0].get('type') == 'text':\\n                    query = contents[0]['text']\\n            \\n            elif event['name'] == 'gen_ai.choice':\\n                body = json.loads(event['body'])\\n                message = body.get('message', {})\\n                contents = message.get('contents', [])\\n                \\n                for content in contents:\\n                    if content.get('type') == 'function_call':\\n                        # Convert to tool call format expected by evaluator\\n                        tool_call = {\\n                            \\\"type\\\": \\\"tool_call\\\",\\n                            \\\"tool_call_id\\\": content.get('call_id', ''),\\n                            \\\"name\\\": content.get('name', ''),\\n                            \\\"arguments\\\": json.loads(content.get('arguments', '{}'))\\n                        }\\n                        tool_calls.append(tool_call)\\n                    \\n                    elif content.get('type') == 'text':\\n                        response = content.get('text', '')\\n        \\n        if query:\\n            # Define tool definitions for weather and time tools\\n            tool_definitions = [\\n                {\\n                    \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_weather\\\",\\n                    \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\", \\n                    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get weather information for a specified location\\\",\\n                    \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n                        \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n                        \\\"properties\\\": {\\n                            \\\"location\\\": {\\n                                \\\"type\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n                                \\\"description\\\": \\\"The location to get weather for\\\"\\n                            }\\n                        },\\n                        \\\"required\\\": [\\\"location\\\"]\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                {\\n                    \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_time\\\", \\n                    \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\",\\n                    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get current UTC time\\\",\\n                    \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n                        \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n                        \\\"properties\\\": {}\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            ]\\n            \\n            evaluation_data.append({\\n                \\\"query\\\": query,\\n                \\\"response\\\": response or \\\"\\\",\\n                \\\"tool_calls\\\": tool_calls,\\n                \\\"tool_definitions\\\": tool_definitions,\\n                \\\"trace_id\\\": trace.get('context', {}).get('trace_id', ''),\\n                \\\"span_id\\\": trace.get('context', {}).get('span_id', '')\\n            })\\n    \\n    # Write to JSONL format\\n    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:\\n        for item in evaluation_data:\\n            f.write(json.dumps(item) + '\\\\n')\\n    \\n    print(f\\\"Converted {len(evaluation_data)} traces to JSONL format: {output_file}\\\")\\n    return output_file\\n\\n\\ndef main():\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Main evaluation function.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    # Set up model configuration for evaluators (using GitHub models for free tier)\\n    model_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\\n        type=\\\"openai\\\",\\n        model=\\\"gpt-4.1-mini\\\",  # Good balance of performance and cost\\n        base_url=\\\"https://models.github.ai/inference\\\",\\n        api_key=os.environ.get(\\\"GITHUB_TOKEN\\\", \\\"your-github-token-here\\\")\\n    )\\n    \\n    # Convert traces to JSONL format\\n    traces_file = \\\"workspace/dataset.json\\\"\\n    jsonl_file = \\\"evaluation_data.jsonl\\\"\\n    \\n    if not os.path.exists(traces_file):\\n        print(f\\\"Error: Dataset file not found: {traces_file}\\\")\\n        sys.exit(1)\\n    \\n    convert_traces_to_jsonl(traces_file, jsonl_file)\\n    \\n    # Initialize evaluators\\n    tool_call_accuracy = ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator(model_config=model_config)\\n    coordination_efficiency = CoordinationEfficiencyEvaluator()\\n    response_completeness = ResponseCompletenessEvaluator()\\n    \\n    # Run evaluation\\n    print(\\\"Starting evaluation of weather-time coordination...\\\")\\n    \\n    try:\\n        result = evaluate(\\n            data=jsonl_file,\\n            evaluators={\\n                \\\"tool_call_accuracy\\\": tool_call_accuracy,\\n                \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": coordination_efficiency,\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": response_completeness\\n            },\\n            evaluator_config={\\n                \\\"tool_call_accuracy\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_calls\\\": \\\"${data.tool_calls}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_definitions\\\": \\\"${data.tool_definitions}\\\",\\n                        \\\"response\\\": \\\"${data.response}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_calls\\\": \\\"${data.tool_calls}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"response\\\": \\\"${data.response}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            },\\n            output_path=\\\"./evaluation_results\\\"\\n        )\\n        \\n        print(\\\"\\\\n\\\" + \\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        print(\\\"EVALUATION RESULTS - Weather & Time Coordination\\\")\\n        print(\\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        \\n        # Print summary metrics\\n        if hasattr(result, 'metrics'):\\n            metrics = result.metrics\\n            print(f\\\"\\\\nOverall Metrics:\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Tool Call Accuracy: {metrics.get('tool_call_accuracy', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Coordination Efficiency: {metrics.get('coordination_efficiency_score', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Response Completeness: {metrics.get('response_completeness_score', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n        \\n        # SDK overview and main components\r\n- \"evaluate\" - Main evaluation API and its parameters\r\n- \"Evaluator\" - Base evaluator classes and patterns\r\n- \"OpenAIModelConfiguration\" - Model configuration examples\r\n- \"_evaluators\" - Built-in evaluators list and usage\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Why Critical**: Without proper SDK understanding, you risk:\r\n- Implementing unnecessary custom evaluators when built-ins exist\r\n- Incorrect evaluator structure leading to runtime errors\r\n- Improper data formatting causing evaluation failures\r\n- Missing key SDK features that optimize performance\r\n\r\n## Core Principles\r\n\r\n- Use Azure AI Evaluation SDK (azure-ai-evaluation)\r\n- Generate a plan before writing code\r\n\r\n## Implement Evaluators\r\n\r\n### Understanding Evaluator Architecture\r\n\r\nAll evaluators in Azure AI Evaluation SDK follow a consistent class structure with two essential methods:\r\n\r\n| Method | Purpose | Details |\r\n|--------|---------|---------|\r\n| `__init__()` | **Setup** | Initializes evaluator with configuration (model settings, parameters, file paths) |\r\n| `__call__()` | **Evaluation Logic** | Processes inputs from your data and returns evaluation results |\r\n\r\n### Choose Your Evaluator Type\r\n\r\nAzure AI Evaluation SDK supports three types of evaluators:\r\n\r\n| Type | Best For | Complexity | Priority |\r\n|------|----------|------------|----------|\r\n| **🔌 Built-in** | Common AI metrics (task adherence, intent resolution, tool accuracy, etc.) | Low | **1st Choice** |\r\n| **🔧 Custom Code-based** | Business-specific objective metrics with custom logic | Medium | 2nd Choice |\r\n| **🤖 Custom Prompt-based** | Business-specific subjective metrics requiring LLM judgment | High | 3rd Choice |\r\n\r\nFor each evaluator you need to implement, follow this decision tree:\r\n\r\n1. **Check Built-in Evaluators First**: Always start by checking if your evaluator can be satisfied via SDK's built-in evaluators\r\n   - ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Create evaluators\r\ntask_adherence_evaluator = TaskAdherenceEvaluator(model_config=model_config) # built-in evaluator\r\nanswer_length_evaluator = AnswerLengthEvaluator() # custom code-based evaluator\r\nfriendliness_evaluator = FriendlinessEvaluator(model_config)\r\n\r\n\r\n# 5. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

Extract tool names from tool calls\\n        weather_tools = []\\n        time_tools = []\\n        other_tools = []\\n        \\n        for call in tool_calls:\\n            if isinstance(call, dict):\\n                name = call.get('name', '')\\n                if 'weather' in name.lower():\\n                    weather_tools.append(call)\\n                elif 'time' in name.lower():\\n                    time_tools.append(call)\\n                else:\\n                    other_tools.append(call)\\n        \\n        has_weather_call = len(weather_tools) > 0\\n        has_time_call = len(time_tools) > 0\\n        total_calls = len(tool_calls)\\n        \\n        # Score based on coordination quality\\n        score = 0.0\\n        reason_parts = []\\n        \\n        if has_weather_call and has_time_call:\\n            score += 3.0  # Base score for using both required tools\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Used both weather and time tools\\\")\\n            \\n            # Check for parallel execution (tools called in same LLM turn)\\n            if len(tool_calls) == 2:  # Optimal case: exactly 2 calls\\n                score += 2.0\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Optimal parallel execution\\\")\\n            elif len(tool_calls) > 2:\\n                score += 1.0  # Some points for parallel but with extra calls\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Parallel execution with extra calls\\\")\\n            else:\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Sequential execution\\\")\\n        elif has_weather_call or has_time_call:\\n            score += 1.0  # Partial score for using one required tool\\n            missing = \\\"time\\\" if has_weather_call else \\\"weather\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(f\\\"Missing {missing} tool call\\\")\\n        else:\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Missing both required tool calls\\\")\\n        \\n        # Efficiency rating\\n        if score >= 4.5:\\n            efficiency = \\\"excellent\\\"\\n        elif score >= 3.0:\\n            efficiency = \\\"good\\\"\\n        elif score >= 1.5:\\n            efficiency = \\\"fair\\\"\\n        else:\\n            efficiency = \\\"poor\\\"\\n        \\n        return {\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": efficiency,\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency_score\\\": score,\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency_reason\\\": \\\"; \\\".join(reason_parts)\\n        }\\n\\n\\nclass ResponseCompletenessEvaluator:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Evaluates whether the response includes both weather and time information when both are requested.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    def __init__(self):\\n        pass\\n    \\n    def __call__(self, *, query: str, response: str, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Union[str, float]]:\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Evaluate response completeness for weather-time coordination queries.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        query_lower = query.lower()\\n        response_lower = response.lower()\\n        \\n        # Check if query requests both weather and time\\n        needs_weather = any(word in query_lower for word in ['weather', 'temperature', 'sunny', 'rain', 'climate'])\\n        needs_time = any(word in query_lower for word in ['time', 'utc', 'clock', 'hour', 'minute', 'when'])\\n        \\n        if not (needs_weather and needs_time):\\n            return {\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": \\\"not_applicable\\\",\\n                \\\"response_completeness_score\\\": 0.0,\\n                \\\"response_completeness_reason\\\": \\\"Query does not require both weather and time\\\"\\n            }\\n        \\n        # Check if response contains weather information\\n        has_weather_info = any(word in response_lower for word in [\\n            'weather', 'temperature', 'sunny', 'rain', 'cloudy', 'degrees', '°c', '°f', 'celsius', 'fahrenheit'\\n        ])\\n        \\n        # Check if response contains time information\\n        has_time_info = any(word in response_lower for word in [\\n            'time', 'utc', 'am', 'pm', 'hour', 'minute', 'clock', ':', 'september', 'monday', 'tuesday'\\n        ]) or any(char.isdigit() and ':' in response for char in response)\\n        \\n        score = 0.0\\n        reason_parts = []\\n        \\n        if has_weather_info and has_time_info:\\n            score = 5.0\\n            completeness = \\\"complete\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Contains both weather and time information\\\")\\n        elif has_weather_info or has_time_info:\\n            score = 2.5\\n            completeness = \\\"partial\\\"\\n            missing = \\\"time\\\" if has_weather_info else \\\"weather\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(f\\\"Contains only {missing} information\\\")\\n        else:\\n            score = 0.0\\n            completeness = \\\"incomplete\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Missing both weather and time information\\\")\\n        \\n        return {\\n            \\\"response_completeness\\\": completeness,\\n            \\\"response_completeness_score\\\": score,\\n            \\\"response_completeness_reason\\\": \\\"; \\\".join(reason_parts)\\n        }\\n\\n\\ndef convert_traces_to_jsonl(traces_file: str, output_file: str) -> str:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Convert OpenTelemetry traces to JSONL format for evaluation.\\n    \\n    Args:\\n        traces_file: Path to the JSON file containing traces\\n        output_file: Path to save the JSONL file\\n    \\n    Returns:\\n        Path to the created JSONL file\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    with open(traces_file, 'r') as f:\\n        data = json.load(f)\\n    \\n    evaluation_data = []\\n    \\n    for trace in data.get('traces', []):\\n        # Extract query from user message event\\n        query = None\\n        response = None\\n        tool_calls = []\\n        \\n        for event in trace.get('events', []):\\n            if event['name'] == 'gen_ai.user.message':\\n                body = json.loads(event['body'])\\n                contents = body.get('contents', [])\\n                if contents and contents[0].get('type') == 'text':\\n                    query = contents[0]['text']\\n            \\n            elif event['name'] == 'gen_ai.choice':\\n                body = json.loads(event['body'])\\n                message = body.get('message', {})\\n                contents = message.get('contents', [])\\n                \\n                for content in contents:\\n                    if content.get('type') == 'function_call':\\n                        # Convert to tool call format expected by evaluator\\n                        tool_call = {\\n                            \\\"type\\\": \\\"tool_call\\\",\\n                            \\\"tool_call_id\\\": content.get('call_id', ''),\\n                            \\\"name\\\": content.get('name', ''),\\n                            \\\"arguments\\\": json.loads(content.get('arguments', '{}'))\\n                        }\\n                        tool_calls.append(tool_call)\\n                    \\n                    elif content.get('type') == 'text':\\n                        response = content.get('text', '')\\n        \\n        if query:\\n            # Define tool definitions for weather and time tools\\n            tool_definitions = [\\n                {\\n                    \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_weather\\\",\\n                    \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\", \\n                    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get weather information for a specified location\\\",\\n                    \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n                        \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n                        \\\"properties\\\": {\\n                            \\\"location\\\": {\\n                                \\\"type\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n                                \\\"description\\\": \\\"The location to get weather for\\\"\\n                            }\\n                        },\\n                        \\\"required\\\": [\\\"location\\\"]\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                {\\n                    \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_time\\\", \\n                    \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\",\\n                    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get current UTC time\\\",\\n                    \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n                        \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n                        \\\"properties\\\": {}\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            ]\\n            \\n            evaluation_data.append({\\n                \\\"query\\\": query,\\n                \\\"response\\\": response or \\\"\\\",\\n                \\\"tool_calls\\\": tool_calls,\\n                \\\"tool_definitions\\\": tool_definitions,\\n                \\\"trace_id\\\": trace.get('context', {}).get('trace_id', ''),\\n                \\\"span_id\\\": trace.get('context', {}).get('span_id', '')\\n            })\\n    \\n    # Write to JSONL format\\n    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:\\n        for item in evaluation_data:\\n            f.write(json.dumps(item) + '\\\\n')\\n    \\n    print(f\\\"Converted {len(evaluation_data)} traces to JSONL format: {output_file}\\\")\\n    return output_file\\n\\n\\ndef main():\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Main evaluation function.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    # Set up model configuration for evaluators (using GitHub models for free tier)\\n    model_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\\n        type=\\\"openai\\\",\\n        model=\\\"gpt-4.1-mini\\\",  # Good balance of performance and cost\\n        base_url=\\\"https://models.github.ai/inference\\\",\\n        api_key=os.environ.get(\\\"GITHUB_TOKEN\\\", \\\"your-github-token-here\\\")\\n    )\\n    \\n    # Convert traces to JSONL format\\n    traces_file = \\\"workspace/dataset.json\\\"\\n    jsonl_file = \\\"evaluation_data.jsonl\\\"\\n    \\n    if not os.path.exists(traces_file):\\n        print(f\\\"Error: Dataset file not found: {traces_file}\\\")\\n        sys.exit(1)\\n    \\n    convert_traces_to_jsonl(traces_file, jsonl_file)\\n    \\n    # Initialize evaluators\\n    tool_call_accuracy = ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator(model_config=model_config)\\n    coordination_efficiency = CoordinationEfficiencyEvaluator()\\n    response_completeness = ResponseCompletenessEvaluator()\\n    \\n    # Run evaluation\\n    print(\\\"Starting evaluation of weather-time coordination...\\\")\\n    \\n    try:\\n        result = evaluate(\\n            data=jsonl_file,\\n            evaluators={\\n                \\\"tool_call_accuracy\\\": tool_call_accuracy,\\n                \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": coordination_efficiency,\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": response_completeness\\n            },\\n            evaluator_config={\\n                \\\"tool_call_accuracy\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_calls\\\": \\\"${data.tool_calls}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_definitions\\\": \\\"${data.tool_definitions}\\\",\\n                        \\\"response\\\": \\\"${data.response}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_calls\\\": \\\"${data.tool_calls}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"response\\\": \\\"${data.response}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            },\\n            output_path=\\\"./evaluation_results\\\"\\n        )\\n        \\n        print(\\\"\\\\n\\\" + \\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        print(\\\"EVALUATION RESULTS - Weather & Time Coordination\\\")\\n        print(\\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        \\n        # Print summary metrics\\n        if hasattr(result, 'metrics'):\\n            metrics = result.metrics\\n            print(f\\\"\\\\nOverall Metrics:\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Tool Call Accuracy: {metrics.get('tool_call_accuracy', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Coordination Efficiency: {metrics.get('coordination_efficiency_score', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Response Completeness: {metrics.get('response_completeness_score', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n        \\n        # Print detailed results if available\\n        if hasattr(result, 'rows'):\\n            print(f\\\"\\\\nDetailed Results:\\\")\\n            for i, row in enumerate(result.rows):\\n                print(f\\\"\\\\n  Query {i+1}: {row.get('query', 'N/A')[:60]}...\\\")\\n                print(f\\\"    Tool Call Accuracy: {row.get('outputs.tool_call_accuracy.tool_call_accuracy', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n                print(f\\\"    Coordination: {row.get('outputs.coordination_efficiency.coordination_efficiency', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n                print(f\\\"    Completeness: {row.get('outputs.response_completeness.response_completeness', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n        \\n        print(f\\\"\\\\nFull results saved to: ./evaluation_results\\\")\\n        print(\\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        \\n    except Exception as e:\\n        print(f\\\"Error during evaluation: {e}\\\")\\n        print(\\\"Please check your GitHub token and model access.\\\")\\n        sys.exit(1)\\n    \\n    # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. the performance of your generative AI applications. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/README.md#L102-L128` starting at line 102:\n````md\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/README.md#L102-L128\n# Azure AI Evaluation client library for Python\n...\n## Key concepts\n\n### Evaluators\n...\n#### Custom evaluators\n\nBuilt-in evaluators are great out of the box to start evaluating your application's generations. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

Extract tool names from tool calls\\n        weather_tools = []\\n        time_tools = []\\n        other_tools = []\\n        \\n        for call in tool_calls:\\n            if isinstance(call, dict):\\n                name = call.get('name', '')\\n                if 'weather' in name.lower():\\n                    weather_tools.append(call)\\n                elif 'time' in name.lower():\\n                    time_tools.append(call)\\n                else:\\n                    other_tools.append(call)\\n        \\n        has_weather_call = len(weather_tools) > 0\\n        has_time_call = len(time_tools) > 0\\n        total_calls = len(tool_calls)\\n        \\n        # Score based on coordination quality\\n        score = 0.0\\n        reason_parts = []\\n        \\n        if has_weather_call and has_time_call:\\n            score += 3.0  # Base score for using both required tools\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Used both weather and time tools\\\")\\n            \\n            # Check for parallel execution (tools called in same LLM turn)\\n            if len(tool_calls) == 2:  # Optimal case: exactly 2 calls\\n                score += 2.0\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Optimal parallel execution\\\")\\n            elif len(tool_calls) > 2:\\n                score += 1.0  # Some points for parallel but with extra calls\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Parallel execution with extra calls\\\")\\n            else:\\n                reason_parts.append(\\\"Sequential execution\\\")\\n        elif has_weather_call or has_time_call:\\n            score += 1.0  # Partial score for using one required tool\\n            missing = \\\"time\\\" if has_weather_call else \\\"weather\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(f\\\"Missing {missing} tool call\\\")\\n        else:\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Missing both required tool calls\\\")\\n        \\n        # Efficiency rating\\n        if score >= 4.5:\\n            efficiency = \\\"excellent\\\"\\n        elif score >= 3.0:\\n            efficiency = \\\"good\\\"\\n        elif score >= 1.5:\\n            efficiency = \\\"fair\\\"\\n        else:\\n            efficiency = \\\"poor\\\"\\n        \\n        return {\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": efficiency,\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency_score\\\": score,\\n            \\\"coordination_efficiency_reason\\\": \\\"; \\\".join(reason_parts)\\n        }\\n\\n\\nclass ResponseCompletenessEvaluator:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Evaluates whether the response includes both weather and time information when both are requested.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    def __init__(self):\\n        pass\\n    \\n    def __call__(self, *, query: str, response: str, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Union[str, float]]:\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        Evaluate response completeness for weather-time coordination queries.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        query_lower = query.lower()\\n        response_lower = response.lower()\\n        \\n        # Check if query requests both weather and time\\n        needs_weather = any(word in query_lower for word in ['weather', 'temperature', 'sunny', 'rain', 'climate'])\\n        needs_time = any(word in query_lower for word in ['time', 'utc', 'clock', 'hour', 'minute', 'when'])\\n        \\n        if not (needs_weather and needs_time):\\n            return {\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": \\\"not_applicable\\\",\\n                \\\"response_completeness_score\\\": 0.0,\\n                \\\"response_completeness_reason\\\": \\\"Query does not require both weather and time\\\"\\n            }\\n        \\n        # Check if response contains weather information\\n        has_weather_info = any(word in response_lower for word in [\\n            'weather', 'temperature', 'sunny', 'rain', 'cloudy', 'degrees', '°c', '°f', 'celsius', 'fahrenheit'\\n        ])\\n        \\n        # Check if response contains time information\\n        has_time_info = any(word in response_lower for word in [\\n            'time', 'utc', 'am', 'pm', 'hour', 'minute', 'clock', ':', 'september', 'monday', 'tuesday'\\n        ]) or any(char.isdigit() and ':' in response for char in response)\\n        \\n        score = 0.0\\n        reason_parts = []\\n        \\n        if has_weather_info and has_time_info:\\n            score = 5.0\\n            completeness = \\\"complete\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Contains both weather and time information\\\")\\n        elif has_weather_info or has_time_info:\\n            score = 2.5\\n            completeness = \\\"partial\\\"\\n            missing = \\\"time\\\" if has_weather_info else \\\"weather\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(f\\\"Contains only {missing} information\\\")\\n        else:\\n            score = 0.0\\n            completeness = \\\"incomplete\\\"\\n            reason_parts.append(\\\"Missing both weather and time information\\\")\\n        \\n        return {\\n            \\\"response_completeness\\\": completeness,\\n            \\\"response_completeness_score\\\": score,\\n            \\\"response_completeness_reason\\\": \\\"; \\\".join(reason_parts)\\n        }\\n\\n\\ndef convert_traces_to_jsonl(traces_file: str, output_file: str) -> str:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Convert OpenTelemetry traces to JSONL format for evaluation.\\n    \\n    Args:\\n        traces_file: Path to the JSON file containing traces\\n        output_file: Path to save the JSONL file\\n    \\n    Returns:\\n        Path to the created JSONL file\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    with open(traces_file, 'r') as f:\\n        data = json.load(f)\\n    \\n    evaluation_data = []\\n    \\n    for trace in data.get('traces', []):\\n        # Extract query from user message event\\n        query = None\\n        response = None\\n        tool_calls = []\\n        \\n        for event in trace.get('events', []):\\n            if event['name'] == 'gen_ai.user.message':\\n                body = json.loads(event['body'])\\n                contents = body.get('contents', [])\\n                if contents and contents[0].get('type') == 'text':\\n                    query = contents[0]['text']\\n            \\n            elif event['name'] == 'gen_ai.choice':\\n                body = json.loads(event['body'])\\n                message = body.get('message', {})\\n                contents = message.get('contents', [])\\n                \\n                for content in contents:\\n                    if content.get('type') == 'function_call':\\n                        # Convert to tool call format expected by evaluator\\n                        tool_call = {\\n                            \\\"type\\\": \\\"tool_call\\\",\\n                            \\\"tool_call_id\\\": content.get('call_id', ''),\\n                            \\\"name\\\": content.get('name', ''),\\n                            \\\"arguments\\\": json.loads(content.get('arguments', '{}'))\\n                        }\\n                        tool_calls.append(tool_call)\\n                    \\n                    elif content.get('type') == 'text':\\n                        response = content.get('text', '')\\n        \\n        if query:\\n            # Define tool definitions for weather and time tools\\n            tool_definitions = [\\n                {\\n                    \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_weather\\\",\\n                    \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\", \\n                    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get weather information for a specified location\\\",\\n                    \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n                        \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n                        \\\"properties\\\": {\\n                            \\\"location\\\": {\\n                                \\\"type\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n                                \\\"description\\\": \\\"The location to get weather for\\\"\\n                            }\\n                        },\\n                        \\\"required\\\": [\\\"location\\\"]\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                {\\n                    \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_time\\\", \\n                    \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\",\\n                    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get current UTC time\\\",\\n                    \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n                        \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n                        \\\"properties\\\": {}\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            ]\\n            \\n            evaluation_data.append({\\n                \\\"query\\\": query,\\n                \\\"response\\\": response or \\\"\\\",\\n                \\\"tool_calls\\\": tool_calls,\\n                \\\"tool_definitions\\\": tool_definitions,\\n                \\\"trace_id\\\": trace.get('context', {}).get('trace_id', ''),\\n                \\\"span_id\\\": trace.get('context', {}).get('span_id', '')\\n            })\\n    \\n    # Write to JSONL format\\n    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:\\n        for item in evaluation_data:\\n            f.write(json.dumps(item) + '\\\\n')\\n    \\n    print(f\\\"Converted {len(evaluation_data)} traces to JSONL format: {output_file}\\\")\\n    return output_file\\n\\n\\ndef main():\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Main evaluation function.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    # Set up model configuration for evaluators (using GitHub models for free tier)\\n    model_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\\n        type=\\\"openai\\\",\\n        model=\\\"gpt-4.1-mini\\\",  # Good balance of performance and cost\\n        base_url=\\\"https://models.github.ai/inference\\\",\\n        api_key=os.environ.get(\\\"GITHUB_TOKEN\\\", \\\"your-github-token-here\\\")\\n    )\\n    \\n    # Convert traces to JSONL format\\n    traces_file = \\\"workspace/dataset.json\\\"\\n    jsonl_file = \\\"evaluation_data.jsonl\\\"\\n    \\n    if not os.path.exists(traces_file):\\n        print(f\\\"Error: Dataset file not found: {traces_file}\\\")\\n        sys.exit(1)\\n    \\n    convert_traces_to_jsonl(traces_file, jsonl_file)\\n    \\n    # Initialize evaluators\\n    tool_call_accuracy = ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator(model_config=model_config)\\n    coordination_efficiency = CoordinationEfficiencyEvaluator()\\n    response_completeness = ResponseCompletenessEvaluator()\\n    \\n    # Run evaluation\\n    print(\\\"Starting evaluation of weather-time coordination...\\\")\\n    \\n    try:\\n        result = evaluate(\\n            data=jsonl_file,\\n            evaluators={\\n                \\\"tool_call_accuracy\\\": tool_call_accuracy,\\n                \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": coordination_efficiency,\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": response_completeness\\n            },\\n            evaluator_config={\\n                \\\"tool_call_accuracy\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_calls\\\": \\\"${data.tool_calls}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_definitions\\\": \\\"${data.tool_definitions}\\\",\\n                        \\\"response\\\": \\\"${data.response}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                \\\"coordination_efficiency\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"tool_calls\\\": \\\"${data.tool_calls}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                },\\n                \\\"response_completeness\\\": {\\n                    \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                        \\\"query\\\": \\\"${data.query}\\\",\\n                        \\\"response\\\": \\\"${data.response}\\\"\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            },\\n            output_path=\\\"./evaluation_results\\\"\\n        )\\n        \\n        print(\\\"\\\\n\\\" + \\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        print(\\\"EVALUATION RESULTS - Weather & Time Coordination\\\")\\n        print(\\\"=\\\"*60)\\n        \\n        # Print summary metrics\\n        if hasattr(result, 'metrics'):\\n            metrics = result.metrics\\n            print(f\\\"\\\\nOverall Metrics:\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Tool Call Accuracy: {metrics.get('tool_call_accuracy', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Coordination Efficiency: {metrics.get('coordination_efficiency_score', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n            print(f\\\"  • Response Completeness: {metrics.get('response_completeness_score', 'N/A')}\\\")\\n        \\n        # In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.\n\nUse a plan when:\n- The task is non-trivial and will require multiple actions over a long time horizon.\n- There are logical phases or dependencies where sequencing matters.\n- The work has ambiguity that benefits from outlining high-level goals.\n- You want intermediate checkpoints for feedback and validation.\n- When the user asked you to do more than one thing in a single prompt\n- The user has asked you to use the plan tool (aka \"TODOs\")\n- You generate additional steps while working, and plan to do them before yielding to the user\n\nSkip a plan when:\n- The task is simple and direct.\n- Breaking it down would only produce literal or trivial steps.\n\nExamples of TRIVIAL tasks (skip planning):\n- \"Fix this typo in the README\"\n- \"Add a console.log statement to debug\"\n- \"Update the version number in package.json\"\n- \"Answer a question about existing code\"\n- \"Read and explain what this function does\"\n- \"Add a simple getter method to a class\"\n\nExamples of NON-TRIVIAL tasks and the plan (use planning):\n- \"Add user authentication to the app\" → Design auth flow, Update backend API, Implement login UI, Add session management\n- \"Refactor the payment system to support multiple currencies\" → Analyze current system, Design new schema, Update backend logic, Migrate data, Update frontend\n- \"Debug and fix the performance issue in the dashboard\" → Profile performance, Identify bottlenecks, Implement optimizations, Validate improvements\n- \"Implement a new feature with multiple components\" → Design component architecture, Create data models, Build UI components, Add integration tests\n- \"Migrate from REST API to GraphQL\" → Design GraphQL schema, Update backend resolvers, Migrate frontend queries, Update documentation\n\n\nPlanning Progress Rules\n- Before beginning any new todo: you MUST update the todo list and mark exactly one todo as `in-progress`. Never start work with zero `in-progress` items.\n- Keep only one todo `in-progress` at a time. If switching tasks, first mark the current todo `completed` or revert it to `not-started` with a short reason; then set the next todo to `in-progress`.\n- Immediately after finishing a todo: you MUST mark it `completed` and add any newly discovered follow-up todos. Do not leave completion implicit.\n- Before ending your turn or declaring completion: ensure EVERY todo is explicitly marked (`not-started`, `in-progress`, or `completed`). If the work is finished, ALL todos must be marked `completed`. Never leave items unchecked or ambiguous.\n\nThe content of your plan should not involve doing anything that you aren't capable of doing (i.e. don't try to test things that you can't test). Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters.
